source.rights_note: Source video and analysis frames were used only as evidence. No source pixels, copied frames, source audio, or expressive source artwork are embedded in the repo example or its MP4. Output is an independently authored abstract ASCII rig preserving only general motion facts and provenance.
source.presentation_cadence_note: The source is explicitly slow motion. OBSERVED timestamps below are source presentation timestamps, not claims about real-world athletic duration or authored exposure cadence.
source.whole_action_inspection: OBSERVED: the entire 13.746 s source was decoded and inspected in order as a 1 fps 14-frame whole-clip sheet before keys were chosen. The coherent throw segment 6.000–12.000 s was then inspected at ordered 2 fps, and the release/forward-arc window 8.000–10.000 s at ordered 4 fps. Source pixels remained analysis-only.

selected_action_preview.sampling: 2 fps ordered 14-frame analysis sheet from 6.000 s

release_window_preview.sampling: 4 fps ordered 9-frame analysis sheet from 8.000 s

observed: The entire 13.746 s source was inspected in order before decisive keys were chosen.
Across 6.000–8.500 s the actor rises and organizes while the visually dominant throwing-limb path travels upward into a clear overhead/high-cock configuration.
Across 8.500–9.000 s the distal limb sweeps rapidly from overhead through a forward diagonal into near-horizontal forward reach.
At 9.000–10.500 s the forward reach persists into a long follow-through/deceleration tail while the torso/root proxy changes less than the distal hand arc.
By 12.000 s the arm has dropped and the actor has re-centered toward a neutral grounded stack.
Ground-adjacent foot support remains visible at the inspected scale throughout the selected segment; no airborne phase is promoted.
No impact event is present in the selected throw segment. Exact hand-ball separation is not visually reliable at the inspected scale and is left UNKNOWN.
inferred: The abstract rig's right_hand channel represents the visually dominant throwing-limb path and is an output-local label, not a claim about anatomical laterality.
Exact foot weight split, pelvis rotation, torso twist, shoulder/elbow angles, and ball-release frame are not pixel-resolved and are not promoted as observed facts.
Transferable principle: a comparatively quiet grounded root/support chain organizes force into a much larger distal overhead-to-forward hand arc, followed by a long deceleration/recovery tail.
Compile cadence is authored with PoseLab FOURS/TWOS/ONES/STREET_FIGHTER-CAPCOM vocabulary because source presentation is slow motion and source-authentic animation exposure classes do not exist.
Connective interpolation changes only joint geometry within an unchanged support/contact semantic state; it never creates a ball, release event, impact, support transfer, or new root decision.
unknown: Exact source frame of hand-ball separation/release
Exact anatomical side identity of the throwing limb
Exact foot weight split or step ownership
Real-world duration represented by the slow-motion presentation

motion_dungeon.transition_rule: Only authored joint geometry interpolates. support_state/contact_note/root_arc_note remain owned by the prior key until the next key. causal_boundary_to_next=true forbids interpolation across unresolved causal/contact/support transitions and holds the prior key until a discrete authored state.
